scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4673: The IT Department reports "switch0 (the IT-dept switch)
failed" -- they say the whole IT segment (192.168.1.0/24) is down because the
access switch connecting the IT hosts to their gateway stopped passing traffic, and
they want the switch replaced/restarted. Please confirm the switch failure.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The IT-segment switch is passing traffic: IT
  hosts (it_hod, it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach
  each other on 192.168.1.0/24. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of an L2 switch failure that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the IT-dept switch (switch0)
failed and took down the IT segment -- is NOT reproducible: IT hosts (it_hod,
it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach each other across
192.168.1.0/24, which means the L2 switch is passing traffic normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the IT-segment switch is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces IT host -> gateway and
host -> host pings, finds them all 0% loss (proving L2 connectivity through the
switch), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a failed switch -- declaring the
IT segment down to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk ticket's premise is incorrect — switch0 has not failed and the IT
segment (192.168.1.0/24) is fully operational. Direct inspection of switch0 shows
both bridge ports (eth0 toward router0 and eth1 toward the IT LAN) are in STP
forwarding state with no errors or drops. The bridge FDB contains freshly learned
MAC entries from both sides: it_hod's MAC (12:da:cf:ff:41:95) on eth1 and
router0's MAC (f6:52:0b:86:6d:2b) on eth0, proving the switch is actively
forwarding frames in both directions.

IT hosts are correctly configured: it_hod holds 192.168.1.2/24 with a default
gateway of 192.168.1.1, matching router0's eth0 address. Live pings from it_hod to
the gateway (192.168.1.1) returned 0% packet loss, and an end-to-end ping from the
IT segment all the way to the servers subnet (pc1, 1.0.0.5) also completed with 0%
loss across three hops, confirming the full forwarding path through switch0,
router0, router1, and router2 is intact. Router0's RIP table shows 192.168.1.0/24
as a directly connected route with reachability to all other segments.

The early observation of TX=0 on it_hod was simply a cold-start artifact (the lab
had just initialized with no user-generated traffic yet); after the first ping,
it_hod immediately showed outbound traffic, confirming there is no transmission
inhibition on the host side either. Root cause: there is no fault — the IT segment
and switch0 are healthy. The ticket is a false alarm; no corrective action is
required.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes IT hosts reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 and each other on 192.168.1.0/24 with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The writeup confirms 0% loss to the gateway but does not explicitly state that IT hosts reach each other on 192.168.1.0/24 with 0% loss.
